new.s: The MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026, passed by the Rajya Sabha in August 2026, provides for which of the following?
o: Abolition of the 45-day payment rule for government buyers
A National Digital Platform for registration and additional State MSE Facilitation Councils
Transfer of delayed-payment disputes from MSEFCs to the NCLT
Replacement of the composite investment-turnover criterion by an employment criterion
new.x: The 2026 Amendment Bill provides a National Digital Platform for registration and additional State MSEFCs. It does not abolish the 45-day rule (that rule continues), does not shift disputes to the NCLT (they go to MSEFCs) and does not change the composite investment-and-turnover criterion to an employment one.
new.tq: 2026 amendment = digital registration platform + more State MSEFCs.

new.s: With reference to TReDS, Budget 2026-27 announced which of the following?
o: TReDS platforms will be regulated by SEBI instead of the RBI
All CPSE purchases from MSMEs are to be settled on TReDS, with CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting
TReDS will be merged with the MSME Samadhaan portal
Only private corporates will be allowed to use TReDS
new.x: Budget 2026-27 mandated settlement of all CPSE purchases from MSMEs on TReDS, CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting, a GeM-TReDS link and receivables as asset-backed securities. TReDS platforms remain RBI-regulated, are not merged with Samadhaan (a delayed-payment portal), and serve government and PSU buyers as well as corporates.
new.tq: Budget 2026-27: CPSE-MSME bills via TReDS + CGTMSE cover + GeM link.

new.s: Between 1 July 2020 and 31 July 2025, how many MSMEs were registered on the Udyam portal (including informal micro enterprises)?
new.x: About 6.63 crore MSMEs were registered on Udyam in that period. Of these, 2.72 crore were informal micro enterprises, so 2.72 crore is only a part. 4.6 crore is not the figure in the notes, and 11 crore is an older employment figure, not a registration count.

new.s: Stand-Up India, launched in April 2016, supports which kind of enterprise?
new.x: Stand-Up India supports only greenfield (new) enterprises promoted by SC/ST persons or women. It is not a rehabilitation scheme for sick units, does not fund expansion of existing units, and has nothing to do with disinvestment of PSEs.
new.tq: Stand-Up India = greenfield only; 51% SC/ST or women.

new.s: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) was set up as a statutory body in:
new.x: KVIC became a statutory body in 1956 under the KVIC Act. 1953 is when its predecessor, the All India Khadi and Village Industries Board, was set up; 1948 is the first Industrial Policy Resolution; 2007 is when the Ministry of MSME was formed.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 covers which period?
new.x: Policy 4.0 covers 2024-29 and was issued through G.O.Ms.No.69 dated 26 October 2024. 2019 is the year of YSR Navodayam, 2020-23 is the period of the earlier Industrial Development Policy, and 2026 is the year of the revamped MSME Policy for women-led units, not a 2026-31 period.
